topics.name: Introduction to DSA and C Setup
subtopics: Writing and Running a C Program

questions.title: Sum of Two Integers
questions.description:
Write and run your first C function. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int sum_two(int a, int b)

It must return the sum of a and b.

Input Format:
One line with two integers A and B.

Output Format:
One line with A + B.

Constraints:
-1000 <= A, B <= 1000

questions.title: Difference and Product
questions.description:
Practise returning computed values from a function.

Implement only this function:

    void diff_prod(int a, int b, int *diff, int *prod)

It must store (a - b) into *diff and (a * b) into *prod. The harness prints both values for you.

Input Format:
One line with two integers A and B.

Output Format:
One line with A - B, then A * B, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= A, B <= 100
questions.topic: Introduction to DSA and C Setup

questions.title: Quotient and Remainder
questions.description:
Use integer division operators.

Implement only this function:

    void div_mod(int a, int b, int *quot, int *rem)

It must store a / b into *quot and a % b into *rem.

Input Format:
One line with two integers A and B (B is never zero).

Output Format:
One line with A / B, then A % B, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= B <= A <= 10000
questions.topic: Introduction to DSA and C Setup

questions.title: Celsius to Fahrenheit
questions.description:
Convert a temperature with a floating-point function.

Implement only this function:

    double celsius_to_fahrenheit(double c)

It must return F where F = C * 9/5 + 32. The harness prints the result rounded to 2 decimals.

Input Format:
One line with a real number C.

Output Format:
One line with the Fahrenheit value rounded to 2 decimals.

Constraints:
-100.0 <= C <= 100.0
questions.topic: Introduction to DSA and C Setup

questions.title: Simple Interest Function
questions.description:
Compute simple interest with the classic formula.

Implement only this function:

    double simple_interest(double p, double r, int t)

It must return (p * r * t) / 100. The harness prints the value rounded to 2 decimals.

Input Format:
One line with the principal P, the annual rate R and the time T in years.

Output Format:
One line with the simple interest rounded to 2 decimals.

Constraints:
1 <= P <= 1000000, 0.1 <= R <= 20.0, 1 <= T <= 30

questions.title: Average of Three Marks
questions.description:
Return a floating-point average from integer inputs.

Implement only this function:

    double average_three(int a, int b, int c)

It must return (a + b + c) / 3.0. The harness prints the result rounded to 2 decimals.

Input Format:
One line with three integer marks A, B and C.

Output Format:
One line with the average rounded to 2 decimals.

Constraints:
0 <= A, B, C <= 100
questions.topic: Introduction to DSA and C Setup

questions.title: Grocery Receipt Total
questions.description:
A small shop prints item totals for its receipts.

Implement only this function:

    double receipt_total(double price, int qty, double taxPercent)

It must return the line total: price * qty, increased by taxPercent percent. The harness prints the value rounded to 2 decimals.

Input Format:
One line with the unit price, the quantity and the tax percent.

Output Format:
One line with the taxed total rounded to 2 decimals.

Constraints:
0.5 <= price <= 10000.0, 1 <= qty <= 500, 0 <= taxPercent <= 30.0

questions.title: Cinema Ticket Cost
questions.description:
A cinema charges 150 rupees per adult ticket and 80 rupees per child ticket.

Implement only this function:

    int ticket_cost(int adults, int children)

It must return adults * 150 + children * 80.

Input Format:
One line with two integers: the number of adults and the number of children.

Output Format:
One line with the total cost in rupees.

Constraints:
0 <= adults, children <= 50, adults + children >= 1

questions.title: Trip Fuel Cost
questions.description:
A delivery van consumes 8 litres of diesel per 100 km; diesel costs L rupees per litre.

Implement only this function:

    double fuel_cost(double km, double litrePrice)

It must return km / 100 * 8 * litrePrice. The harness prints the value rounded to 2 decimals.

Input Format:
One line with the trip distance in km and the price per litre.

Output Format:
One line with the fuel cost rounded to 2 decimals.

Constraints:
1 <= km <= 2000, 50 <= litrePrice <= 150

questions.title: Hostel Mess Bill
questions.description:
A hostel bills Veg meals at 60 rupees and Non-Veg meals at 95 rupees per day.

Implement only this function:

    int mess_bill(int vegDays, int nonvegDays)

It must return vegDays * 60 + nonvegDays * 95.

Input Format:
One line with two integers: veg days and non-veg days.

Output Format:
One line with the total mess bill.

Constraints:
0 <= vegDays, nonvegDays <= 31

questions.title: Currency Denomination Split
questions.description:
An ATM splits an amount into 500- and 100-rupee notes with as many 500s as possible.

Implement only this function:

    void split_notes(int amount, int *fifties, int *hundreds)

It must store the number of 500-rupee notes into *fifties (wait — the harness names them generically): store amount / 500 into *fifties and (amount % 500) / 100 into *hundreds. Amounts are always multiples of 100.

Input Format:
One line with the amount.

Output Format:
One line with the count of 500-notes, then the count of 100-notes, space-separated.

Constraints:
100 <= amount <= 100000, amount % 100 == 0
questions.topic: Introduction to DSA and C Setup

questions.title: Seconds to Clock Parts
questions.description:
A timer converts a raw second count into hours, minutes and seconds.

Implement only this function:

    void to_clock(int total, int *h, int *m, int *s)

It must store total / 3600 into *h, (total % 3600) / 60 into *m and total % 60 into *s.

Input Format:
One line with the total seconds.

Output Format:
One line with h, m and s space-separated.

Constraints:
0 <= total <= 86399

questions.title: Digit Sum of a Three-Digit Number
questions.description:
A checksum routine sums the digits of a three-digit code.

Implement only this function:

    int digit_sum3(int n)

It must return the sum of the three decimal digits of n (100 <= n <= 999).

Input Format:
One line with the integer n.

Output Format:
One line with the digit sum.

Constraints:
100 <= n <= 999

questions.title: Swap via Pointers
questions.description:
A sort utility needs an in-place swap helper built on pointers.

Implement only this function:

    void swap_ints(int *a, int *b)

It must exchange the values pointed to by a and b (use a temporary).

Input Format:
One line with two integers.

Output Format:
One line with the two values after the swap, space-separated.

Constraints:
-1000 <= values <= 1000

questions.title: Series and Parallel Resistance
questions.description:
A lab tool reports both the series and the parallel resistance of two resistors.

Implement only this function:

    void resistance(double r1, double r2, double *series, double *parallel)

It must store r1 + r2 into *series and (r1 * r2) / (r1 + r2) into *parallel. The harness prints both rounded to 3 decimals.

Input Format:
One line with two resistances.

Output Format:
One line with the series value, then the parallel value, space-separated, each rounded to 3 decimals.

Constraints:
0.1 <= r1, r2 <= 10000.0
questions.topic: Introduction to DSA and C Setup

questions.title: Last Digit and Digit Stripping
questions.description:
A roll-number validator extracts the last digit and the remaining prefix.

Implement only this function:

    void last_digit(int n, int *prefix, int *digit)

It must store n / 10 into *prefix and n % 10 into *digit.

Input Format:
One line with the roll number n (at least two digits).

Output Format:
One line with the prefix, then the last digit, space-separated.

Constraints:
10 <= n <= 999999

questions.title: Grade Classifier
questions.description:
An exam system maps an integer score to a letter grade:
90-100 → A, 75-89 → B, 60-74 → C, 40-59 → D, below 40 → F.

Implement only this function:

    char grade_of(int score)

It must return the grade character ('A', 'B', 'C', 'D' or 'F').

Input Format:
One line with the score.

Output Format:
One line with the grade letter.

Constraints:
0 <= score <= 100

questions.title: Compound Interest Without pow
questions.description:
A savings app computes yearly compound interest WITHOUT calling pow (it targets a bare-bones build).

Implement only this function:

    double compound_interest(double p, double r, int years)

It must return the growth amount only: p * (1 + r/100)^years - p, computed with a loop. The harness prints the value rounded to 2 decimals.

Input Format:
One line with the principal, the annual percent rate and the number of years.

Output Format:
One line with the compound growth rounded to 2 decimals.

Constraints:
1 <= p <= 1000000, 1 <= r <= 15.0, 1 <= years <= 25

questions.title: Triangle Type Classifier
questions.description:
A geometry tool classifies a triangle from its three side lengths:
EQUILATERAL when all sides are equal, ISOSCELES when exactly two sides are equal, SCALENE otherwise. The input always forms a valid triangle.

Implement only this function:

    const char *triangle_type(int a, int b, int c)

It must return one of the three strings above (string literals are fine).

Input Format:
One line with the three side lengths.

Output Format:
One line with EQUILATERAL, ISOSCELES or SCALENE.

Constraints:
1 <= a, b, c <= 1000

questions.title: Tiered Taxi Fare
questions.description:
A city taxi meters the fare in tiers: the first 2 km cost a flat 50 rupees; every whole km beyond that costs 18 rupees; a 20 percent night surcharge applies when the flag is set. Fractional extra kilometres are charged only for each COMPLETED km (floor).

Implement only this function:

    double taxi_fare(double km, int night)

It must return the fare: 50 + floor(km - 2) * 18 when km > 2, else 50; multiply the total by 1.2 when night is non-zero. Return 0 when km <= 0. The harness prints the fare rounded to 2 decimals.

Input Format:
One line with the distance and the night flag (0 or 1).

Output Format:
One line with the fare rounded to 2 decimals.

Constraints:
0 <= km <= 500, night is 0 or 1
